goal_residuals.summary: This unit closes the process named-import wall. The other I6 walls stay with map items 2 (path subpaths), 4 (loud members), 5 (guard precision) and 10 (vm offsets). End-to-end proof is map item 12.
Still open through map items 1, 6-9, 11 and 13. End-to-end acceptance is map item 12.

coverage.row: Acceptance 1: `import { cwd } from 'node:process'` links, and the imported cwd() called unbound equals process.cwd(). RED at BASE: link SyntaxError on `cwd`
coverage.note: The case catches the link failure: RED at BASE (evidence R3), GREEN at HEAD. It does not catch the 'called unbound' part. Scratch mutant M5 made `cwd` depend on its receiver (`cwd = function (this) { if (this === undefined) throw …; return cwd(); }`), and esm-named-members still passed, because rifty's ESM transform calls an imported binding with a receiver (`__m0(...).cwd()`). The shipped `cwd` ignores `this` (packages/runtime-js/src/builtins/process.ts:144), and a browser probe ran a real unbound alias call (`const f = cwd; f()` → TINY|true, exit 0). Advisory only.

coverage.row: Acceptance 2: cwd/chdir/hrtime/uptime/exit/kill/nextTick are own data properties with writable, enumerable and configurable all true. exitCode is an own accessor, enumerable and non-configurable. Each name is in Object.keys(process), links with ns[name] === process[name], and hrtime.bigint stays own
Acceptance 3: in a forked child, detached exit(3) closes with code 3 and detached kill(pid,'SIGUSR2') closes with signal SIGUSR2, with no stderr. RED at BASE: TypeError, code 1

Acceptance 4: named imports of on/emit/addListener/prependListener/removeListener/removeAllListeners/listenerCount/pushStdin fail to link with a SyntaxError that names the export, and none of them is own on process
Parity case 1: Node v24.16.0 output of process/esm-named-members (evidence O3)
Parity case 2: Node output of process/esm-named-members-off-surface, 8x SyntaxError:true plus 8 false own flags (evidence O4)
Parity case 3: Node output of process/unbound-exit-kill, code 3 and signal SIGUSR2 with stderr false (evidence O5)

findings.evidence: Scratch worktree at e8ca0c17e, process.ts:489 changed to `cwd = function (this: NodeProcess): string { if (this === undefined) throw new TypeError("unbound"); return cwd(); };`, then `pnpm test:parity process/esm-named-members` → `✓ process/esm-named-members-off-surface.case.ts`, `✓ process/esm-named-members.case.ts`, `all cases match`. Browser-unit probe (Chromium, sealed workbench, node tinyexec-like.mjs containing `import { cwd } from 'node:process'; const f = cwd; f()`) → `{"exit":0,"out":"TINY|true\n"}`.
findings.summary: No committed carrier makes a truly unbound call to an imported process member on the rifty side: the loader passes a receiver to import calls (a divergence that predates this unit). Acceptance 1's 'called unbound' holds only because the delivered cwd/chdir/hrtime/uptime ignore `this` (process.ts:144-189). An alias call (`const f = cwd; f()`) in the case would catch this; that is an advisory hardening.

Carried over from Contract+RED. Acceptance 2's descriptor exactness and Acceptance 3 trace only to ADR-0348, and its §2 states only the enumerable-keys naming rule. The carriers catch every part anyway: M1 (non-bound exit/kill → unbound-exit-kill code 1/stderr true), M2 (exitCode configurable:true), M3 (exitCode non-enumerable) and M4 (`hrtime.bind(null)` → `hrtime.bigint is not a function`) all fail. Acceptance 5 (compat row + CHANGELOG) traces to a rule id only, so it gets no coverage row; both are present (docs/public/compat/process.md:27, packages/runtime-js/CHANGELOG.md:5).

Map item 3 still describes the rejected prototype-walk mechanism. Contract Decision line 68 gives the edit to the land step; keep it on the land checklist. RDY-8 preparation is present: the Contract+RED JSON is committed with reviewed_sha 5f355a654 and blockers.mjs exits 0. Since that SHA the contract has gained only the ready-verdict and IMPLEMENT decision lines, and the parity cases are unchanged. goal.md and ledger.md are untouched.

`declare exitCode: number` narrows the TypeScript setter type from `unknown` to `number`. At runtime the setter still coerces numeric strings and throws on invalid values (process.ts:517-524). This is type-level only, on the internal `./builtins/process` subpath.

findings.summary: Three pre-existing divergences found during this unit have no backlog item yet. D1 (a non-IPC process over-exports send/disconnect/connected/channel/_listenersMap/_warned) is at least stated in the compat row. D2 (a self SIGUSR2 with a live listener terminates the process instead of running the listener) and the import-call receiver divergence are not in the compat page. The compat row says `kill(process.pid, 'SIGUSR2')` works without noting D2. The driver must route all three before landing (REV-12, rifty-to-backlog) so they do not become a silent backlog.
